status: Original candidate prompts; educator comparability review pending; no learner responses
instructions: Aim for 60–100 words, but do not penalize shorter accessible responses automatically. Invent details; do not disclose personal information. Prompt families suggest opportunities, not guaranteed skill elicitation. Assign baseline and transfer tasks before viewing outcomes; use the remaining task for delayed transfer.

prompts.text: Describe how an imaginary school library works each morning. Explain what one librarian does and what a group of pupils does.
Describe how an imaginary community garden is cared for each day. Explain what one caretaker does and what a group of volunteers does.
Describe how an imaginary sports club prepares for practice. Explain what one coach does and what the players do.

families.candidate_focus: Past narration with legitimate changes of time frame

prompts.text: Imagine a class trip was delayed yesterday. Explain what happened, how the group responded, and one thing they will do differently next time.
Imagine a team could not use its usual playground last week. Explain what happened, how they solved the problem, and their plan for next week.
Imagine rain interrupted an outdoor book fair last month. Explain what happened, what the organisers did, and what they plan for the next fair.

families.candidate_focus: Position, relevant reason and explanation without invented authority

prompts.text: A school can open a quiet reading room or an indoor games room during lunch. Recommend one choice and explain why it would help pupils. No statistics or research are required.
A community centre can run a weekend art club or a weekend sports club. Recommend one choice and explain why it would help children. No statistics or research are required.
A class can spend its activity hour making a garden or producing a small magazine. Recommend one choice and explain why it would help classmates. No statistics or research are required.
